nodes.title: Connection pool
nodes.summary: Wikipedia article defining a connection pool as a cache of reusable database connections, kept by the client or by middleware, to avoid the overhead of opening and closing connections.

nodes.title: Exponential backoff
nodes.summary: Wikipedia article on exponential backoff: an algorithm that uses feedback to multiplicatively decrease the rate of a process until it finds an acceptable rate, used widely in computer and wireless networks.

nodes.title: Infrastructure as code
nodes.summary: Wikipedia article on infrastructure as code: managing and provisioning infrastructure through machine-readable definition files, often kept in version control and usually declarative, instead of manual or interactive configuration.

nodes.title: Multitenancy
nodes.summary: English Wikipedia article on software multitenancy: one instance of software serving several tenants, each with a dedicated share of data, configuration and user management. It contrasts multitenancy with multi-instance architectures, where each tenant gets a separate software instance.

nodes.title: Observability (software)
nodes.summary: Wikipedia article describing observability as the ability to collect data about a program's execution, internal state and communication between components, using logging and tracing, and as the first step in triaging an outage. One stated goal is to reduce the prior knowledge needed to debug.

nodes.title: Postmortem documentation
nodes.summary: Wikipedia article on project post-mortems: a process to identify the causes of a project failure and how to prevent them, distinguished from a retrospective, which reviews both positive and negative aspects.

nodes.title: Rate limiting
nodes.summary: Short Wikipedia article on rate limiting: controlling the rate of requests sent or received by a network interface, used for example against denial-of-service attacks and web scraping.

nodes.title: Service-level objective
nodes.summary: Wikipedia article defining an SLO as a target value or range for a service level measured by a service level indicator (SLI), commonly part of a service-level agreement, and also used internally by organizations practicing SRE.

nodes.title: Shard (database architecture)
nodes.summary: Wikipedia article on database sharding: a shard is a horizontal partition of data, and each shard may sit on a separate database server to spread load.

nodes.title: Site reliability engineering
nodes.summary: Wikipedia article on SRE: a discipline that monitors and improves the availability and performance of deployed software, with emphasis on automation and infrastructure as code, and overlapping with DevOps in its goals.

nodes.title: Thundering herd problem
nodes.summary: Wikipedia article on the thundering herd problem: many processes or threads are woken at once for an event or a newly available resource, only one can use it, and the rest fail and go back to sleep, wasting resources and slowing the one that succeeds.
